profile.summary: RFamLlama is a generative RNA language model conditioned on RNA family. Given an Rfam family ID as a prompt tag, it writes new RNA sequences of that family; the same model can also score sequences for zero-shot fitness prediction. It was trained on sequences from over 4,000 RNA families, each labelled with a family tag.

summary_quotes.text: we introduce RFamLlama, a conditional language model that is specifically optimized for generating RNA sequences across diverse families.
allowing for the generation of RNA sequences by using Rfam IDs as input prompts, thereby eliminating the need for further functional-specific fine-tuning.
This model was trained on RNA sequences representing over 4,000 distinct families, each augmented with control tags to denote the specific family.
We have shown that the inclusion of family-specific tags substantially enhances the capabilities of our model in zero-shot fitness prediction of RNA molecules.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: RFamLlama is a decoder-only Llama model for causal (next-token) language modelling over a 22-token vocabulary. Each training sequence is preceded by a control tag naming its family. A prompt has the form <|bos|> <|tag_start|> family number <|tag_end|> <|5|>, where the family number is the Rfam ID without the RF prefix; the model then writes the sequence, which ends at the <|3|> token. The developers report that the family tags improve zero-shot fitness prediction; the sources read do not say how a fitness score is computed.
sections.source_locator: config.json (base); model card usage code; abstract

quotes.text: each augmented with control tags to denote the specific family.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: Two checkpoints are published: RFamLlama-base (8 layers, hidden size 512, 31,488,512 parameters) and RFamLlama-large (10 layers, hidden size 768, 88,523,520 parameters). Both use the same tokenizer and prompt format. Generation is sampled (do_sample=True), so a result should name the checkpoint, its revision and the sampling settings.
sections.source_locator: config.json of each checkpoint; Hugging Face API safetensors totals; model card usage code

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Family-conditioned autoregressive RNA language model for sequence generation and zero-shot fitness prediction.

quotes.text: RFamLlama is poised to be an effective and widely applicable tool for the zero-shot fitness prediction and generation of RNA sequences

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Llama decoder. Base: 8 layers, hidden size 512, intermediate size 2048, 32 attention heads, 16 key-value heads. Large: 10 layers, hidden size 768, intermediate size 3072, 32 attention heads, 16 key-value heads.

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: A prompt holding an Rfam family number between tag tokens, for example <|bos|> <|tag_start|> 00005 <|tag_end|> <|5|> for RF00005.

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: Generated RNA sequences, read from the text between the <|5|> and <|3|> tokens and printed in FASTA style in the card example.

facts.label: Parameters
facts.value: RFamLlama-base: 31,488,512 (31.5M). RFamLlama-large: 88,523,520 (88.5M). Both counted from the safetensors files.

facts.label: Training data
facts.value: RNA sequences from over 4,000 families, each with a family control tag. The card refers to the families by Rfam ID; the exact Rfam release and sequence count are not stated.

run_guide.summary: Load RFamLlama-base from Hugging Face and sample ten tRNA-family (RF00005) sequences.
prerequisites: Python with PyTorch and transformers; the sources give no versions or install command. The checkpoints were saved with transformers 4.38.2.
A CUDA GPU is used when available; otherwise the example runs on CPU.

steps.title: Generate sequences for one Rfam family
steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
# generation
from transformers import LlamaForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer, pipeline
import torch
import sys

model_url = "jinyuan22/RFamLlama-base"
model = LlamaForCausalLM.from_pretrained(model_url, torch_dtype=torch.float16)
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_url)

device = torch.device("cuda:0") if torch.cuda.is_available() else torch.device("cpu")

pipe = pipeline("text-generation", model=model, device=device, tokenizer=tokenizer)

tag = "RF00005"
txt = f"<|bos|> <|tag_start|> {tag[2:]} <|tag_end|> <|5|> "
all_outputs = []
outputs = pipe(txt, num_return_sequences=10, max_new_tokens=300, repetition_penalty=1, top_p=1,temperature=1, do_sample=True)

for i, output in enumerate(outputs):
    seq = output["generated_text"]
    seq = seq.split("<|5|>")[1].split("<|3|>")[0]
    print(f">{i}\n{seq}")
PY
steps.explanation: The model card's example, wrapped in a shell heredoc. Replace RF00005 with another Rfam ID, or the model URL with jinyuan22/RFamLlama-large, to change family or size. It downloads the latest revision.

outputs: Ten sampled sequences printed in FASTA style, with headers >0 to >9.
limitations: This command was read from the model card and has not been executed by Rewire.
Outputs are random samples and change between runs unless a seed is set; the card sets none.
